meta.name: Tesela Studio
meta.title: Tesela Studio · AI products people actually trust
meta.tagline: An editorial site for an AI product studio: calm, precise, gallery-like.
meta.description: Tesela Studio is a fictional AI product studio that designs agents, copilots and AI features for companies. A business-services demo with a scroll-driven hero, sample case studies, sticky process panels, a dark theme and an in-page project brief.
features: Sticky scroll-driven hero with an isometric landscape
Case studies in a dialog with their own URL
Stacked process panels and flipping letter tiles in pure CSS
Project brief in a dialog with validation and its own URL

a11y.landscape: Illustration: stacks of isometric cubes that fit together

hero.lead: A small studio that turns a messy process into an agent, a copilot or a feature your team uses every day. Strategy, interface and evaluation, in weeks.
hero.after: Every piece fits before it ships.

services.title: What we do
services.lead: Four disciplines, one team. We take a problem from the whiteboard to the people who'll use it.

items.title: Product strategy
items.text: We find the process where AI saves the most hours and where a mistake costs the least, then define what success looks like.

items.title: Agents and automation
items.text: Assistants that read your documents, fill in your systems and ask a person before they do anything that can't be undone.

items.title: Interfaces people trust
items.text: Drafts you can edit, visible sources, clear confidence levels. People keep using it because they understand it.

items.title: Evaluation and safety
items.text: Hundreds of real cases scored before launch, quality alerts afterwards and a human handoff when it isn't sure.

work.title: Selected work
work.lead: Three projects, three industries. Each one solved a process that used to eat whole days.

items.name: Pliego
items.text: A contract review assistant for a mid-sized law firm: it flags risky clauses and drafts the reply with its sources.
items.problem: Associates spent their afternoons comparing supplier contracts against the firm's standard terms, clause by clause.
built: Review panel that sits next to the document
Clause comparison against the firm's playbook
Reply draft with a citation for every change
items.stack: Document pipeline · retrieval over the playbook · evaluation set of 400 clauses

items.name: Rutero
items.text: A dispatch copilot for a food distributor: it proposes tomorrow's routes and explains every change to the driver.
items.problem: Two dispatchers rebuilt routes by hand every night, juggling late orders, time windows and refrigerated trucks.
built: Route proposal with reasons in plain words
items.stack: Route optimiser · language model for explanations · integration with the order system

items.name: Acopio
items.text: A reorder agent for a grocery chain: it forecasts demand per store and prepares orders that a buyer approves.
items.problem: Each store manager ordered from memory. Some shelves ran empty on Fridays while others threw away fresh produce.
built: Daily forecast per store and product
Draft orders with a confidence level
items.stack: Forecasting models · ordering agent with human approval · weekly evaluation

dialog.outcomeNote: Sample figures for a fictional case.

process.title: How a project moves
process.lead: From the first conversation to the whole company using it. You see something working every week.

steps.title: We find where it pays off
steps.text: Interviews, shadowing and your real data. We rank processes by hours saved and by the cost of a mistake.

steps.title: A prototype you can use
steps.text: Not slides: a working version with your documents, so the team can break it and tell us where it falls short.

steps.title: We measure before we launch
steps.text: Hundreds of real cases scored one by one. If it doesn't hit the bar, it doesn't ship. If it hesitates, it hands over to a person.

steps.title: Launch in steps
steps.text: One pilot team first, then everyone. With monitoring, quality alerts and a monthly review with you.

formats.title: Ways to work together
formats.lead: Start small and grow only if the numbers say so.

items.name: Discovery sprint
items.text: Opportunity map, one clickable prototype and an honest go or no-go.

items.name: Pilot
items.text: A working version with your data, an evaluation set and a pilot team using it.

items.name: Embedded team
items.text: Design, engineering and evaluation working with your team, with releases every month.
